state: Sellers control immediate direction as price extends a bearish run through the latest broken low floor.
paragraphs: Sellers are currently holding immediate control of the market as price action extends a bearish run measuring 6 bricks down to the 1.139 level. The confirmed swing structure fully agrees with this downward pressure, showing a sequence of lower highs and lower lows that aligns cleanly with the bearish momentum. The break matters because the market has successfully pushed below the latest confirmed low floor at 1.1455, removing that immediate price protection. Even though sellers are pressing forward, the overall control remains messy and unstable with alternating movement across the broader picture. The bearish read weakens if buyers manage to develop consistent upward runs and stable timing to reverse this latest downward extension.

Recent downward movement is expanding in size while opposing upside progress remains severely constrained. The broader history across 104 bricks shows a balanced baseline where bullish and bearish runs historically averaged 2.52 and 2.32 bricks respectively, with identical counts of 21 bullish and 22 bearish runs. However, recent behavior has shifted notably as selling pressure takes a deeper footprint. Looking at the latest 12 runs, bearish expansions average 3.5 bricks while opposing upward attempts struggle to muster an average of just 1.33 bricks. The longest bearish run in this recent window matches the peak downward stretch of 6 bricks, whereas the longest bullish recovery spans only 2 bricks. This imbalance highlights how downward extensions are growing while upward counters fail to gain traction.

The current downward move cannot be trusted as a clean trend yet because chaotic background conditions and erratic timing continue to dominate the background. Control repeatedly shifts back and forth without establishing a stable directional state, reflected in a heavy balance score of 94.5 and a high transition score of 75.3. Even though selling pressure has intensified recently, low opposing wick pressure of 5.5 and inconsistent timing across the 104 bricks show that neither side holds steady follow-through. The move can keep extending if directional expansion escapes the persistent chop, but until timing consistency improves and rapid state switching subsides, this remains an unstable transition rather than a reliable trend.

The first support area sitting directly below current price is the 1.1385 confirmed low pivot, with deeper backing found at the 1.13531 harmonic level and the 1.13458 bollinger lower boundary. The first area overhead is clustered around the 1.143 confirmed high pivot and the 1.14295 bollinger middle boundary. This zone also holds the broken confirmed low floor at 1.1455, which now acts as immediate resistance after giving way during the latest downward extension. Further up, the neutral sar level at 1.14808 and the bollinger upper boundary at 1.15132 provide the next layers of overhead defense. The larger trend barrier is defined much higher up by the falling regression line at 1.16086, keeping a firm lid on any broader recovery attempts.

The move can keep extending if sellers continue pressing into open space without facing meaningful pushback, backed by low opposing wick pressure of 5.5 and a contracting volatility envelope that shows momentum is no longer expanding forcefully behind the decline. At the same time, counter-pressure is present as a developing bull Bat pattern approaches its 1.139 harmonic completion point alongside a harmonic X point at 1.13531. However, this pattern acts as counter-pressure rather than a confirmed reversal while underlying timing consistency remains low. The bearish read weakens if buyers manage to secure sustained recoveries off these support layers and break the persistent market chop.

Current market action remains in an unstable transition because rapid state switching and erratic timing continue to dictate the background. The setup stays unresolved as long as short alternating runs and mixed wicks persist without a stable replacement state. Current control would look more convincing if rapid state switching intensified alongside frequent local flips and conflicting wicks. Conversely, the read weakens if either side manages to gain coherent pace control and establish a stable directional range. Genuine structural change requires a clear shift away from this disorderly balance score of 94.5 and low timing consistency into an orderly, sustained directional trend.
